policy_title: Rooftop Solar Revolution and Fair Price for Electricity
stated: Drive a rooftop solar revolution by expanding incentives for households to install solar panels, including a guaranteed fair price for electricity sold back into the grid.

source.quote: Drive a rooftop solar revolution by expanding incentives for households to install solar panels, including a guaranteed fair price for electricity sold back into the grid.

bearing_set.reason: Expanding solar incentives and a guaranteed grid sell-back price directly affect household energy bills — a core cost-of-living indicator — for those who install panels, and may affect wider energy prices depending on scheme funding mechanism.
Scaling rooftop solar generation displaces fossil-fuel electricity, directly bearing on the UK's emissions trajectory and clean-energy transition.

Rooftop solar incentives predominantly benefit homeowners with sufficient capital and suitable roof space (historically higher-income households), while any cost recovery through levies or taxation can fall on all bill-payers including renters, creating a concrete regressive distributional mechanism that moves the rich-poor gap indicator.

membership_note: Three fundamentals with clear, mechanistic links: a clean-environment benefit (O6), an energy-cost benefit for participating households (O2), and a plausible inequality cost via skewed uptake and potential socialised funding (O14). Fiscal effects (O12) are possible if incentives are unfunded at scale but the policy text gives no funding mechanism, so O12 does not clear the non-negligible bar without further detail.
